answer: The local radio environment is a fingerprint: an agent scans the spectrum around it and submits a signed snapshot of towers and beacons, and the registry checks it against the known radio map of the claimed spot, like an island whose signals pass through a prism that bends them one way only. A relic of an old scan cannot be replayed, because the snapshot must be fresh, so a Sybil farm on one bench cannot claim a thousand cells.
